LTE or Wi-Fi: what fits your site?
LTE or Wi-Fi Reader? A Site Checklist | SmartphoneKey
How to choose between LTE and Wi-Fi access control readers: what both share, what differs and what to check at each door before ordering.
getting_started

Choose by the connection each door can rely on. A Wi-Fi reader suits doors with reliable Wi-Fi on a network you can configure as the installation guide describes. An LTE reader suits doors with reliable cellular coverage, where you can provide a SIM and service. Both readers work with the same platform, include the access controller and need power, compatible lock hardware and wiring.
/products/readers,/find-your-setup,/compatibility

div.h2: What both readers have in common

ul.li: They work with the same Admin Panel, so sites, people, keys and cards are managed the same way.
The access controller is built into the reader.
Each can act as a Thread Border Router and as a router in the Thread mesh, without a separate firmware version.
Each needs power, compatible lock hardware and the wiring described in the installation and connection guide.

div.p: The main difference is the connection each reader depends on.
LTE and Wi-Fi reader comparison.
div.h2: What is decided for each project

ul.li: Which doors get an LTE reader and which get a Wi-Fi reader.
Which reader version suits the region where it is installed. Ask us before ordering.
Which reader connects the Thread mesh to the internet, and what the site does if that connection drops.

div.p: With an LTE reader, someone provides the SIM and cellular service, keeps it active and checks coverage at the position where the reader will be mounted.

With a Wi-Fi reader, the reader joins the site's own network. The network owner provides the access details, keeps the network configured as the installation guide describes, and tells you before the network name, password or equipment change.

ul.li: Cellular coverage measured at each planned reader position, not just outside the building.
Who supplies the SIM and service, and in which region the reader is installed.
Who renews the service and who is told if it stops.
Wi-Fi coverage at each planned reader position.
Who owns and manages the network, and whether it restricts new devices.
How you will hear about changes to the network name, password or equipment.

div.h2: When to ask for a site review
div.p: Ask us to review the site when coverage at a reader position is uncertain, when doors are in basements or behind heavy construction, when several buildings are planned together, or when a third party manages the network. Coverage depends on the building, placement and radio conditions, so it is checked on site rather than promised in advance.
Choose the connection that fits the site, then confirm the reader version for your region with us.

Which NFC cards can SmartphoneKey program?
MIFARE Classic and MIFARE DESFire EV3 Cards | SmartphoneKey
Supported SmartphoneKey reader configurations program MIFARE Classic and MIFARE DESFire EV3 cards. How it works and what to check before ordering.
cards_devices

Supported SmartphoneKey reader configurations also let you program MIFARE Classic and MIFARE DESFire EV3 cards. An administrator starts the programming in the Admin Panel, then taps the card on a SmartphoneKey reader that supports programming. Reading a card, programming it, assigning access and using it at a door are separate operations. Confirm other card generations, memory sizes and existing credential formats with us before ordering.

div.h2: Reading, programming, assigning and using a card
div.p: Four separate operations involve a card:

ul.li: Reading: a reader detects the card and its identifier.
Programming: a SmartphoneKey reader that supports programming writes a SmartphoneKey credential to a supported card.
Assigning access: the Admin Panel links the card to a person and to the doors they may open.
Using the card: the person holds the card to a reader at a door they have access to.

div.p: A card that a reader can detect is not automatically a card that SmartphoneKey can program.

div.h2: How an administrator programs a card

ol.li: In the Admin Panel, choose the site, the person and the doors the card is for.
Choose the card type: MIFARE Classic or MIFARE DESFire EV3.
When the Admin Panel asks, tap the card on the SmartphoneKey reader that supports programming.
Check the result in the Admin Panel before you hand the card over.

div.p: The Admin Panel user guide describes each screen.

Cards are programmed with a SmartphoneKey reader that supports programming; SmartphoneKey does not support third-party card programmers. Card programming is available on supported reader configurations, so ask us which configuration to plan for your site.
div.h2: Why other generations and sizes need confirmation
div.p: Cards within one family share a common basis, but chip-level compatibility does not show that SmartphoneKey can program every generation, memory size or credential format. The same applies to other card types and to cards that already carry another system's credentials.
Before ordering, send us the exact card product, its memory size and any credential format already on it. Please do not send keys or card secrets.

Matter and Thread for access control
Matter and Thread in Access Control | SmartphoneKey
What Matter, Thread and a Thread Border Router each do, which Thread roles SmartphoneKey readers take, and what to settle before planning a mesh.
networks_automation

Matter describes what a connected device can do, such as switch on or report a temperature. Thread is an IP mesh network that Matter devices can use, and a Thread Border Router connects that mesh to your other IP networks. Every SmartphoneKey reader can act as a Thread Border Router and as a router in the mesh, without a separate firmware version. What a scenario can do depends on the capabilities each device reports.
/platform/automation,/compatibility,/products/readers
Connectivity Standards Alliance: Matter | https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/ OpenThread: Border Router | https://openthread.io/guides/border-router

div.h2: Four roles that are easy to confuse

tr.td: Reports capabilities such as on/off, contact or temperature
That every controller can use every function
Commissions devices and sends them commands
That it forwards Thread traffic
Forwards traffic inside the Thread mesh
That the mesh can reach the internet
Connects the Thread mesh to other IP networks
That it controls Matter devices

div.p: Every SmartphoneKey reader can act as a Thread Border Router and as a Thread router, without a separate firmware version. Which reader carries the mesh's connection to the internet is decided for each site. Matter controller functions are confirmed for each project, and the roles of other devices depend on their own hardware and firmware.
Example topology. Deployment depends on configuration.

ol.li: The site's internet connection, over Wi-Fi, Ethernet or a cellular network.
A Thread Border Router, which links the Thread mesh to that network. Any SmartphoneKey reader can take this role.
Thread routers, which pass traffic between devices in the mesh. Every SmartphoneKey reader can take this role too.
Matter devices, such as sensors, lights and valves, each reporting its own capabilities.
A Matter controller, which commissions the devices and runs the configured scenarios.

div.h2: Capabilities decide what a scenario can do
div.p: A Matter label does not mean every device offers the same functions. A contact sensor reports open or closed; a light switches on or off; a leak sensor reports water; a valve opens or closes; a thermostat accepts a setpoint. A scenario can use only what the commissioned device reports and what your configuration supports.
Each scenario currently belongs to one hub and the devices commissioned to it. Plan scenarios around the hub that controls the devices they need.
div.h2: Coverage and the route to the internet
div.p: A mesh depends on the roles of its devices, their placement and power, and the route to the internet. Coverage depends on the building, placement and radio conditions, so plan it for the site and check it after installation. When the route to the internet is lost, remote management waits for it to return; read what happens when a reader goes offline.
div.h2: Questions to settle for your site

ul.li: Which reader version and firmware will be installed?
Which readers will connect the mesh to the internet, and which other devices join the mesh?
How does the site reach the internet, and what should happen if that connection drops?
Which devices and capabilities does each scenario need, and which hub controls them?

access-control-when-offline
What happens when a reader goes offline?
Access Control When a Reader Is Offline | SmartphoneKey
What happens to key changes while a reader is offline: pending and confirmed states, revocation, local access and what to check after reconnecting.
operating

Some changes you make in the Admin Panel wait until the reader reconnects. A pending change has not reached the reader yet, so a revocation made while a reader is offline is not in effect there until the reader confirms it. Whether keys and cards keep working at the door during an outage depends on the device and its configuration. Check the status of a change before you rely on it.
/platform/access-management,/security,/products/readers

tr.td: The change was made in the Admin Panel.
Follow its status.
The change is waiting for the reader to reconnect. It is not on the reader yet.
Treat the previous access as still possible on that reader.
The reader reported that it applied the change.
For an unlock, this shows the reader acted. It does not prove a person passed through or the door opened.
The reader reported an error, or no confirmation arrived.
Check the reader and its connection, then repeat the change or contact support.

div.p: Not every kind of change waits in the queue: some need the reader to be online when you make them.

A revocation made while a reader is offline is pending, not enforced. Until the reader reconnects and confirms the change, the key or card may still work on that reader. When access must end at once, restore the reader's connection, watch for the confirmation and follow your site's own procedures in the meantime.

ul.li: The reader's connection status.

Device alerts, if you have configured them.

div.p: Whether keys and cards keep working at the door during an outage depends on the device and its configuration. Other services rely on the connection in their own ways: the QR intercom, video, AI Concierge and issuing new keys or cards do not share one outage behaviour, so check each one you depend on.

When the reader reconnects, queued changes are delivered and their status updates. If a change stays unconfirmed, contact support with the site and reader details. Please do not send passwords or access codes by email.
